strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5N01 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: interpret, compare and order numbers with more than 2 decimal places, including numbers greater than one, using place value understanding; represent these on a number line

elaborations.name: VC2M5N01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: making models of decimals including tenths, hundredths and thousandths by subdividing materials or grids, and explaining the multiplicative relationship between consecutive places; for example, explaining that thousandths are 10 times smaller than hundredths, or writing numbers into a place value chart to compare and order them

elaborations.name: VC2M5N01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: renaming decimals to assist with mental computation; for example, when asked to solve 0.6 ÷ 10 they rename 6 tenths as 60 hundredths and say, ‘If I divide 60 hundredths by 10, I get 6 hundredths’ and write 0.6 ÷ 10 = 0.06

elaborations.name: VC2M5N01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a number line or number track to represent and locate decimals with varying numbers of decimal places and numbers greater than one and justifying the placement; for example, 2.335 is halfway between 2.33 and 2.34, that is, 2.33 < 2.335 < 2.34, and 5.283 is between 5.28 and 5.29 but closer to 5.28

elaborations.name: VC2M5N01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting and comparing the digits in decimal measures, for example, the length or mass of animals or plants, such as a baby echidna weighing 1.78 kilograms and a platypus weighing 1.708 kilograms

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS1
organising_ideas.text: All lifeforms are connected through Earth’s systems (the lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere), on which they depend for their wellbeing and survival.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

elaborations.name: VC2M5N01-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting plans or diagrams showing length measures as decimals, placing the numbers into a decimal place value chart to connect the digits to their value

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5N02 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: express natural numbers as products of their factors, recognise multiples and determine if one number is divisible by another

elaborations.name: VC2M5N02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a certain number of blocks to form different rectangles and using these to list all possible factors for that number; for example, 12 blocks can form the following rectangles: 1 × 12, 2 × 6 and 3 × 4

elaborations.name: VC2M5N02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching divisibility tests and explaining each rule using materials; for example, using base-10 blocks to test if numbers are divisible by 2, 5 and 10

elaborations.name: VC2M5N02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using divisibility tests to determine if larger numbers are multiples of one-digit numbers; for example, testing if 89 472 is divisible by 3 using 8 + 9 + 4 + 7 + 2 = 30, as 30 is divisible by 3 then 89 472 is a multiple of 3

elaborations.name: VC2M5N02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating and reasoning that all multiples can be formed by combining or regrouping; for example, multiples of 7 can be formed by combining a multiple of 2 with the corresponding multiple of 5: 3 × 7 = 3 × 2 + 3 × 5, and 4 × 7 = 4 × 2 + 4 × 5

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5N03 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: compare and order common unit fractions with the same and related denominators, including mixed numerals, applying knowledge of factors and multiples; represent these fractions on a number line

elaborations.name: VC2M5N03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using pattern blocks to represent equivalent fractions; selecting one block or a combination of blocks to represent one whole, and making a design with shapes; and recording the fractions to justify the total

elaborations.name: VC2M5N03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a fraction wall from paper tape to model and compare a range of different fractions with related denominators, and using the model to play fraction wall games

elaborations.name: VC2M5N03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting a fraction wall model and a number line model of fractions to say how they are the same and how they are different; for example, explaining $\frac{1}{4}$ on a fraction wall represents the area of one-quarter of the whole, while on the number line $\frac{1}{4}$ is identified as a point that is one-quarter of the distance between zero and one

elaborations.name: VC2M5N03-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an understanding of factors and multiples as well as equivalence to recognise efficient methods for the location of fractions with related denominators on parallel number lines; for example, explaining on parallel number lines that $\frac{2}{10}$ is located at the same position on a parallel number line as $\frac{1}{5}$ because $\frac{1}{5}$ is equivalent to $\frac{2}{10}$

elaborations.name: VC2M5N03-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: converting between mixed numerals and improper fractions to assist with locating them on a number line

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5N04 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: recognise that 100% represents the complete whole and use percentages to describe, represent and compare relative size; connect familiar percentages to their decimal and fraction equivalents

elaborations.name: VC2M5N04-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising applications of percentages used in everyday contexts, for example, the bar model used for charging devices indicating the percentage of power remaining, and advertising in retail contexts relating to discounts or sales

elaborations.name: VC2M5N04-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a model by subdividing a whole (for example, using 10 × 10 grids to represent various percentage amounts) and recognising complementary percentages (such as 30% and 70%) combine to make 100%

elaborations.name: VC2M5N04-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a model by subdividing a collection of materials, such as blocks or money, to connect decimals and percentage equivalents of tenths and the commonly used fractions $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{1}{4}$ and $\frac{3}{4}$; for example, connecting that one-tenth or 0.1 represents 10% and one-half or 0.5 represents 50%, and recognising that 60% of a whole is 10% more of the whole than 50%

elaborations.name: VC2M5N04-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using physical and virtual materials to represent the relationship between decimal notation and percentages, for example, 0.3 is 3 out of every 10, which is 30 out of every 100, which is 30%

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5N05 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with the same or related denominators, using different strategies

elaborations.name: VC2M5N05-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using different ways to add and subtract fractional amounts by subdividing different models of measurement attributes; for example, adding half an hour and three-quarters of an hour using a clock face, adding a $\frac{3}{4}$ cup of flour and a $\frac{1}{4}$ cup of flour, subtracting $\frac{3}{4}$ of a metre from 2 $\frac{1}{4}$ metres

elaborations.name: VC2M5N05-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing and solving addition and subtraction problems involving fractions by using jumps on a number line, or bar models, or making diagrams of fractions as parts of shapes

elaborations.name: VC2M5N05-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using materials, diagrams, number lines or arrays to show and explain that fraction number sentences can be rewritten in equivalent forms without changing the quantity, for example, $\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}$ is the same as $\frac{2}{4}+\frac{1}{4}$

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5N06 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: solve problems involving multiplication of larger numbers by one- or two-digit numbers, choosing efficient mental and written calculation strategies and using digital tools where appropriate; check the reasonableness of answers

elaborations.name: VC2M5N06-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: solving multiplication problems such as 253 × 4 using a doubling strategy, for example, 2 × 253 = 506 and 2 × 506 = 1012

elaborations.name: VC2M5N06-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: solving multiplication problems like 15 × 16 by thinking of factors of both numbers, 15 = 3 × 5, 16 = 2 × 8, and rearranging the factors to make the calculation easier, 5 × 2 = 10, 3 × 8 = 24 and 10 × 24 = 240

elaborations.name: VC2M5N06-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an array to show place value partitioning to solve multiplication, such as 324 × 8, thinking 300 × 8 = 2400, 20 × 8 = 160, 4 × 8 = 32 then adding the parts, 2400 + 160 + 32 = 2592; and connecting the parts of the array to a standard written algorithm

elaborations.name: VC2M5N06-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using different strategies used to multiply numbers, and explaining how they work and if they have any limitations; for example, discussing how the Japanese visual method for multiplication is not effective for multiplying larger numbers

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASK1
organising_ideas.text: Peoples of the Asia region are diverse in their backgrounds, experiences, traditions, cultures, histories, stories, religions, beliefs, perspectives and languages.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU1
organising_ideas.text: The nations of Asia influence historical and contemporary global relationships, including international responses to global developments and events.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

organising_ideas.name: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia - VC2CCPASU2
organising_ideas.text: The peoples of Asia shape human endeavour through the arts and political, sporting, economic, technological and scientific domains.
organising_ideas.ccp: Asia and Australia’s Engagement with Asia

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5N07 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: solve problems involving division, choosing efficient mental and written strategies and using digital tools where appropriate; interpret any remainder according to the context and express results as a whole number, decimal or fraction

elaborations.name: VC2M5N07-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting and solving everyday division problems such as ‘How many buses are needed if there are 436 passengers and each bus carries 50 people?’, deciding whether to round up or down in order to accommodate the remainder and justifying choices

elaborations.name: VC2M5N07-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: solving division problems mentally, such as 72 divided by 9, 72 ÷ 9, by thinking, ‘How many nines make 72?’, □ x 9 = 72, or ‘Share 72 equally 9 ways’

elaborations.name: VC2M5N07-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the fact that equivalent division calculations result if both numbers are divided by the same factor

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5N08 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: check and explain the reasonableness of solutions to problems, including financial contexts using estimation strategies appropriate to the context

elaborations.name: VC2M5N08-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting a series of contextual problems to decide whether an exact answer or an approximate calculation is appropriate, and explaining their reasoning in relation to the context and the numbers involved

elaborations.name: VC2M5N08-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the effect of rounding addition, subtraction, multiplication and division calculations, and rounding both numbers up, both numbers down, and one number up and one number down; and explaining which estimation is the best approximation and why

elaborations.name: VC2M5N08-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: considering the type of rounding that is appropriate when estimating the amount of money required; for example, rounding up or rounding down when buying one item from a store using cash, compared to rounding up the cost of every item when buying groceries to estimate the total cost and not rounding when the financial transactions are digital

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5N09 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving additive and multiplicative situations, including simple financial planning contexts; formulate the problems, choosing operations and efficient mental and written calculation strategies, and using digital tools where appropriate; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation

elaborations.name: VC2M5N09-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: modelling an everyday situation and determining which operations can be used to solve it using materials, diagrams, arrays and/or bar models to represent the problem; formulating the situation as a number sentence; and justifying their choice of operations in relation to the situation

elaborations.name: VC2M5N09-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: modelling a series of contextual problems, deciding whether an exact answer or an approximate calculation is appropriate, and explaining their reasoning in relation to the context and the numbers involved

elaborations.name: VC2M5N09-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: modelling financial situations such as creating financial plans; for example, creating a budget for a class fundraising event, using a spreadsheet to tabulate data and perform calculations

elaborations.name: VC2M5N09-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating how mathematical models involving combinations of operations can be used to represent songs, stories and/or dances of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5N10 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: follow a mathematical algorithm involving branching and repetition (iteration); create and use algorithms involving a sequence of steps and decisions and digital tools to experiment with factors, multiples and divisibility; identify, interpret and describe emerging patterns

elaborations.name: VC2M5N10-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: simulating a simple random walk

elaborations.name: VC2M5N10-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: manipulating sets of numbers using a given rule, for example, if a number is even, halve it; or if a number is odd, subtract 1 then halve it

elaborations.name: VC2M5N10-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating algorithms that use multiplication and division facts to determine if a number is a multiple or factor of another number; for example, using a flow chart that determines whether numbers are factors or multiples of other numbers using branching, such as yes/no decisions

elaborations.name: VC2M5N10-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying lowest common multiples and highest common factors of pairs or triples of natural numbers; for example, the lowest common multiple of {6, 9} is 18, and the highest common factor is 3, and the lowest common multiple of {3, 4, 5} is 60 and the highest common factor is 1

elaborations.name: VC2M5N10-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the ‘fill down’ function of a spreadsheet and a multiplication formula to generate a sequence of numbers that represent the multiples of any number you enter into the cell, and describing and explaining the emerging patterns

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5A01 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and explain the connection between multiplication and division as inverse operations and use this to develop families of number facts

elaborations.name: VC2M5A01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using materials or diagrams to develop and explain division strategies, such as halving, using the inverse relationship to turn division into a multiplication

elaborations.name: VC2M5A01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using arrays, multiplication tables, and physical and virtual materials to develop families of facts, for example, 3 × 4 = 12, 4 × 3 = 12, 12 ÷ 3 = 4 and 12 ÷ 4 = 3

elaborations.name: VC2M5A01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating multiplicative partitioning using materials, diagrams or arrays and recording 2 multiplication and 2 division facts for each grouping (for example, 4 × 6 = 24, 6 × 4 = 24, 24 ÷ 4 = 6 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4), explaining how each grouping is different from and connected to other groupings in the materials, diagrams or arrays

elaborations.name: VC2M5A01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using materials, diagrams or arrays to recognise and explain the inverse relationship between multiplication and division (for example, solving 240 ÷ 20 = □ by thinking 20 × □ = 240) and using the inverse to make calculations easier (for example, solving 17 × □ = 221 using division, □ = 221 ÷ 17)

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5A02 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: find unknown values in numerical equations involving multiplication and division using the properties of numbers and operations

elaborations.name: VC2M5A02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using knowledge of equivalent number sentences to form and find unknown values in numerical equations; for example, given that 3 × 5 = 15 and 30 ÷ 2 = 15, then 3 × 5 = 30 ÷ 2, and therefore the solution to 3 × 5 = 30 ÷ □ is 2

elaborations.name: VC2M5A02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using relational thinking, and an understanding of equivalence and number properties to determine and reason about numerical equations; for example, explaining whether an equation involving equivalent multiplication number sentences is true, such as 15 ÷ 3 = 30 ÷ 6

elaborations.name: VC2M5A02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using materials, diagrams and arrays to demonstrate that multiplication is associative and commutative but division is not – for example, using arrays to demonstrate that 2 × 3 = 3 × 2 but 6 ÷ 3 does not equal 3 ÷ 6; demonstrating that 2 × 2 × 3 = 12 and 2 × 3 × 2 = 12 and 3 × 2 × 2 = 12; and understanding that 8 ÷ 2 ÷ 2 = (8 ÷ 2) ÷ 2 = 2 but 8 ÷ (2 ÷ 2) = 8 ÷ 1 = 8

elaborations.name: VC2M5A02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using materials, diagrams or arrays to recognise and explain the distributive property, for example, where 4 × 13 = 4 × 10 + 4 × 3

elaborations.name: VC2M5A02-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing equivalent number sentences involving multiplication to form a numerical equation, and applying knowledge of factors, multiples and the associative property to find unknown values in numerical equations; for example, considering 3 × 4 = 12 and knowing 2 × 2 = 4, then 3 × 4 can be written as 3 × (2 × 2) and, using the associative property, (3 × 2) × 2 so 3 × 4 = 6 × 2 and so 6 is the solution to 3 × 4 = □ × 2

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5M01 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: choose appropriate metric units when measuring the length, mass and capacity of objects; use smaller units or a combination of units to obtain a more accurate measure

elaborations.name: VC2M5M01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: ordering metric units from the largest unit to the smallest, for example, kilometre, metre, centimetre, millimetre

elaborations.name: VC2M5M01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that some units of measurement are better suited to some tasks than others; for example, kilometres are more appropriate than metres to measure the distance between 2 towns

elaborations.name: VC2M5M01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: deciding on the unit required to estimate the amount of paint or carpet for a room or a whole building, and justifying the choice of unit in relation to the context and the degree of accuracy required

elaborations.name: VC2M5M01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: measuring and comparing distances (for example, measuring and comparing jumps or throws using a metre length of string and then measuring the part metre with centimetres and/or millimetres) and explaining which unit of measure is most accurate

elaborations.name: VC2M5M01-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: researching how the base units are derived for the International System of Units (SI), commonly known as the metric system of units, recognising that the metric unit names for the attributes of length and mass are international standards for measurement

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5M02 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: solve practical problems involving the perimeter and area of regular and irregular shapes using appropriate metric units

elaborations.name: VC2M5M02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating problem situations involving perimeter, for example, ‘How many metres of fencing are required around a paddock, or around a festival event?’

elaborations.name: VC2M5M02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using efficient ways to calculate the perimeters of rectangles, such as adding the length and width together and doubling the result

elaborations.name: VC2M5M02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: solving measurement problems such as ‘How much carpet would be needed to cover the entire floor of the classroom?’, using square metre templates to directly measure the floor space

elaborations.name: VC2M5M02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a model of a permaculture garden, dividing the area up to provide the most efficient use of space for gardens and walkways, labelling the measure of each area, and calculating the amount of resources needed, for example, compost to cover the vegetable garden

elaborations.name: VC2M5M02-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a physical geoboard or a virtual geoboard app to recognise the relationship between area and perimeter and solve problems; for example, investigating what is the largest and what is the smallest area that has the same perimeter

elaborations.name: VC2M5M02-E06 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring the designs of fishing nets and dwellings of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, investigating the perimeter, area and purpose of the shapes within the designs

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5M03 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: compare 12- and 24-hour time systems and solve practical problems involving the conversion between them

elaborations.name: VC2M5M03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using timetables written in 24-hour time, such as flight schedules, to plan an overseas or interstate trip, converting between 24- and 12-hour time

elaborations.name: VC2M5M03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: converting between the digital and analog representation of 24-hour time, matching the same times represented in both systems; for example, setting the time on an analog watch from a digital alarm clock

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5M04 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: estimate, construct and measure angles in degrees, using appropriate tools, including a protractor, and relate these measures to angle names

elaborations.name: VC2M5M04-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a protractor to measure angles in degrees and classifying these angles using angle names; for example, an acute angle is less than 90°, an obtuse angle is more than 90° and less than 180°, a right angle is equal to 90° and a reflex angle is more than 180° and less than 360°

elaborations.name: VC2M5M04-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: estimating the size of angles in the environment using a clinometer and describing the angles using angle names

elaborations.name: VC2M5M04-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a ruler and protractor to construct triangles, given the angle measures and side lengths

elaborations.name: VC2M5M04-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a protractor to measure angles when creating a pattern or string design within a circle

elaborations.name: VC2M5M04-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the size of angles within shapes that do and do not tessellate, measuring the angles and using the sum of angles to explain why some shapes will tessellate and other shapes do not

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5SP01 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: connect objects to their nets and build objects from their nets using spatial and geometric reasoning

elaborations.name: VC2M5SP01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing and constructing exact nets for packaging particular-shaped items or collections of interest, taking into consideration how the faces will be joined and how the package will be opened

elaborations.name: VC2M5SP01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: visualising folding some possible nets for a range of prisms and pyramids, predicting which will work and which cannot work, and justifying their choices, based on the number, size and position of particular shapes in each diagram

elaborations.name: VC2M5SP01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: sketching nets for a range of prisms and pyramids considering the number, shape and placement of the faces, and testing by cutting and folding

elaborations.name: VC2M5SP01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating objects designed and developed by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Peoples, such as those used in fish traps and instructive toys, identifying the shape and relative position of each face to determine the net of the object

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5SP02 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: construct a grid coordinate system that uses coordinates to locate positions within a space; use coordinates and directional language to describe position and movement

elaborations.name: VC2M5SP02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding how the numbers on the axes on a grid coordinate system are numbers on a number line and are used to pinpoint locations

elaborations.name: VC2M5SP02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the conventions of indicating a point in a grid coordinate system; for example, writing the horizontal axis number first and the vertical axis number second, and using brackets and commas

elaborations.name: VC2M5SP02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing a grid reference system to a grid coordinate system (first quadrant only) by using both to play strategy games involving location; for example, in playing the game Quadrant Commander, deducing that in a grid coordinate system the lines are numbered (starting from zero), not the spaces

elaborations.name: VC2M5SP02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: placing a coordinate grid over a contour line, drawing and listing the coordinates of each point in the picture, asking a peer to re-create the drawing using only the list of coordinates, and discussing the reasons for the potential similarities and differences between the 2 drawings

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5SP03 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: describe and perform translations, reflections and rotations of shapes, using dynamic geometry software where appropriate; recognise what changes and what remains the same, and identify any symmetries

elaborations.name: VC2M5SP03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding and explaining that translations, rotations and reflections can change the position and orientation of a shape but not its shape or size

elaborations.name: VC2M5SP03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using pattern blocks and paper, tracing around a shape and then conducting a series of one-step transformations and tracing each resulting image, and then finally copying the original position and end position on a new sheet of paper

elaborations.name: VC2M5SP03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating how different combinations of transformations can produce the same resulting image

elaborations.name: VC2M5SP03-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: challenging classmates to select a combination of transformations to move from an original image to the final image, noting the different combinations by using different colours to trace images

elaborations.name: VC2M5SP03-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating how animal tracks can be interpreted by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples using the transformation of their shapes, to help determine and understand animal behaviour

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5ST01 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: acquire, validate and represent data for nominal and ordinal categorical and discrete numerical variables to address a question of interest or purpose using software including spreadsheets; discuss and report on data distributions in terms of highest frequency (mode) and shape, in the context of the data

elaborations.name: VC2M5ST01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that ordinal data is a form of categorical data even though the data being collected might be numbers, for example, a rating scale using numbers 1–5 to represent the categories people can choose from when asked, ‘What rating would you give this film out of 5?’

elaborations.name: VC2M5ST01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: determining the mode for a set of data and discussing that there may be more than one mode

elaborations.name: VC2M5ST01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the best methods of presenting data to illustrate the results of investigations and justifying the choice of representations

elaborations.name: VC2M5ST01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: acquiring data through chance experiments, discussing and reporting on the distribution of outcomes and how this relates to equal and unequal outcomes

elaborations.name: VC2M5ST01-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using digital systems to validate data; for example, recognising the difference between numerical, text and date formats in spreadsheets, and setting data types in a spreadsheet to make sure a date is input correctly

elaborations.name: VC2M5ST01-E06 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating data relating to the reconciliation process between Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples and non-Indigenous Australians, posing questions, discussing and reporting on findings

organising_ideas.text: The occupation and colonisation of the land now known as Australia by the British, under the now overturned doctrine of terra nullius, were experienced by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples as an invasion that denied their occupancy of, and connection to, Country and Place.

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5ST02 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: interpret line graphs representing change over time; discuss the relationships that are represented and conclusions that can be made

elaborations.name: VC2M5ST02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: reading and interpreting different line graphs, discussing how the horizontal axis represents measures of time such as days of the week or times of the day, and the vertical axis represents numerical quantities or ordinal categorical variables such as percentages, money, measurements or ratings such as fire hazard ratings

elaborations.name: VC2M5ST02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting real-life data represented as a line graph showing how measurements change over a period of time, and make simple inferences

elaborations.name: VC2M5ST02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: matching unlabelled line graphs to the context they represent based on the stories of the different contexts

elaborations.name: VC2M5ST02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting the data represented in a line graph, making inferences; for example, reading line graphs that show the varying temperatures or ultraviolet (UV) rates over a period of a day and discussing when would be the best time to hold an outdoor assembly

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSFT1
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable futures thinking is based on informed views that consider possible and desirable futures. It leads to individual, community, organisational and political action that reduces risk.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSFT3
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable futures thinking requires individuals to think creatively, seek information, identify a variety of possibilities, reflect and evaluate actions, and collaborate with and influence others as they work towards desired futures.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M5ST03 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: plan and conduct statistical investigations by posing questions or identifying a problem and collecting relevant data; choose appropriate displays and interpret the data; communicate findings within the context of the investigation

elaborations.name: VC2M5ST03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: posing questions about insect diversity in the playground, and collecting data by taping a one-metre-square piece of paper to the playground and observing the type and number of insects on it over time

elaborations.name: VC2M5ST03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: posing a question or identifying a problem of interest; collecting, interpreting and analysing the data; and discussing if the data generated provides the information necessary to answer the question

elaborations.name: VC2M5ST03-E03 - Mathematics

elaborations.name: VC2M5P01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing what it means for outcomes to be equally likely and comparing the number of possible and equally likely outcomes of chance events; for example, when drawing a card from a standard deck of cards there are 4 possible outcomes if you are interested in the suit, 2 possible outcomes if you are interested in the colour or 52 outcomes if you are interested in the exact card

elaborations.name: VC2M5P01-E02 - Mathematics

elaborations.name: VC2M5P01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: commenting on the chance of winning games by considering the number of possible outcomes and the consequent chance of winning

elaborations.name: VC2M5P01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating why some games are fair and others are not; for example, drawing a track game to resemble a running race and taking it in turns to roll 2 dice, where the first runner moves a square if the difference between the 2 dice is zero, one or 2 and the second runner moves a square if the difference is 3, 4 or 5, and responding to the questions ‘Is this game fair?’, ‘Are some differences more likely to come up than others?’ and ‘How can you work that out?’

elaborations.name: VC2M5P01-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the chance of a head or a tail when a coin is tossed, whether some numbers on a dice are more likely to be facing up when the dice is rolled, or the chance of getting a 1, 2 or 3 on a spinner with uneven regions for the numbers

elaborations.name: VC2M5P01-E06 - Mathematics

elaborations.name: VC2M5P02-E01 - Mathematics

elaborations.name: VC2M5P02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: conducting experiments, recording the outcomes and the number of times the outcomes occur, and describing the relative frequency of each outcome; for example, using ‘I threw the coin 10 times, and the results were 3 times for a head, so that is 3 out of 10, and 7 times for a tail, so that is 7 out of 10’

elaborations.name: VC2M5P02-E03 - Mathematics

elaborations.name: VC2M5P02-E04 - Mathematics

elaborations.name: VC2M5P02-E05 - Mathematics

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Level 6, learning in Mathematics builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences. Students engage in a range of approaches to the learning and doing of mathematics that develop their understanding of and fluency with concepts, procedures and processes by making connections, reasoning, problem-solving and practice. Proficiency in mathematics enables students to respond to familiar and unfamiliar situations by employing mathematical strategies to make informed decisions and solve problems efficiently.

Students further develop proficiency and positive dispositions towards mathematics and its use as they:

  • expand the repertoire of numbers they work with to include rational numbers and the use of integers in practical contexts, such as locating points in the 4 quadrants of a Cartesian plane
  • extend their knowledge of factors and multiples to understand the properties of prime, composite, triangular and square numbers
  • solve arithmetic problems involving all 4 operations with natural numbers of any size
  • use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems, choosing models, representations and calculation strategies, and justify solutions
  • apply computational thinking approaches to develop algorithms that use rules to generate numbers
  • develop a range of written and digital means for representing objects and three-dimensional spaces in 2 dimensions
  • apply their understanding of area and use multiplicative thinking to establish the formula for the area of a rectangle
  • begin to formally use deductive reasoning in spatial contexts involving lines and angles
  • describe and compare probabilities numerically
  • determine the mode and range and discuss the shape of distributions in their reports of findings from their statistical investigations
  • observe and compare long-run frequencies in repeated chance experiments and simulations.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 6, students use integers to represent points on a number line and on the Cartesian plane. They solve problems using the properties of prime, composite, square and triangular numbers. Students order common fractions, giving reasons, and add and subtract fractions with related denominators. They use all 4 operations with decimals and connect decimal representations of measurements to the metric system. Students solve problems involving finding a fraction, decimal or percentage of a quantity and use estimation to find approximate solutions to problems involving rational numbers and percentages. They use mathematical modelling to solve financial and other practical problems involving percentages and rational numbers, formulating and solving the problem, and justifying choices.

Students find unknown values in numerical equations involving combinations of arithmetic operations. They identify and explain rules used to create growing patterns. They design and use algorithms to generate sets of numbers, using a rule.

Students interpret and use timetables, and measure, calculate and compare elapsed time. They convert between common units of length, mass and capacity. They use the formula for the area of a rectangle and angle properties to solve problems.

Students identify the parallel cross-section for right prisms. They create tessellating patterns using combinations of transformations. They locate an ordered pair in any one of the 4 quadrants on the Cartesian plane.

Students compare distributions of discrete and continuous numerical and ordinal categorical data sets as part of their statistical investigations, using digital tools. They critique arguments presented in the media based on statistics.

Students assign probabilities using common fractions, decimals and percentages. They conduct simulations using digital tools, to generate and record the outcomes from many trials of a chance experiment. They compare observed frequencies to the expected frequencies of the outcomes of chance experiments.

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E01
as_extracts.description: students use integers to represent points on a number line and on the Cartesian plane.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N01 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: recognise situations, including financial contexts, that use integers; locate and represent integers on a number line and as coordinates on the Cartesian plane

elaborations.name: VC2M6N01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: extending the number line in the negative direction to locate and represent integers, recognising the difference in location between (−2) and (+2) and their relationship to zero as −2 < 0 < 2

elaborations.name: VC2M6N01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using integers to represent quantities in financial contexts, including the concept of profit and loss for a planned event

elaborations.name: VC2M6N01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using horizontal and vertical number lines to represent and find solutions to everyday problems involving locating and ordering integers around zero (for example, elevators, above and below sea level) and distinguishing a location by referencing the 4 quadrants of the Cartesian plane

elaborations.name: VC2M6N01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that the sign (positive or negative) indicates a direction in relation to zero – for example, 30 metres left of the admin block is (−30) and 20 metres right of the admin block is (+20) – and programming robots to move along a number line that is either horizontal or vertical but not both at the same time

elaborations.name: VC2M6N01-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing the temperatures of the different planets in the solar system, using a diagram of a thermometer that models a vertical number line

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E02
as_extracts.description: They solve problems using the properties of prime, composite, square and triangular numbers.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N02 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: identify and describe the properties of prime, composite, square and triangular numbers and use these properties to solve problems and simplify calculations

elaborations.name: VC2M6N02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the definition of a prime number to explain why one is not a prime number

elaborations.name: VC2M6N02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: testing numbers by using division to distinguish between prime and composite numbers, recording the results on a number chart to identify any patterns

elaborations.name: VC2M6N02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing composite numbers as a product of their factors, including prime factors when necessary and using this form to simplify calculations involving multiplication, such as 15 × 16 as 5 × 3 × 4 × 4, which can be rearranged to simplify calculation to 5 × 4 × 3 × 4 = 20 × 12

elaborations.name: VC2M6N02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and describing the product of a number with itself as square; for example, 3 × 3 is the same as $3^{2}$

elaborations.name: VC2M6N02-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using spreadsheets to list all the numbers that have up to 3 factors, using combinations of only the first 3 prime numbers, recognising any emerging patterns, making conjectures and experimenting with other combinations

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E03
as_extracts.description: Students order common fractions, giving reasons, and add and subtract fractions with related denominators.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N03 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: apply knowledge of equivalence to compare, order and represent common fractions, including halves, thirds and quarters, on the same number line and justify their order

elaborations.name: VC2M6N03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying factors and multiples to fraction denominators (such as halves with quarters, eighths and twelfths, and thirds with sixths, ninths and twelfths) to determine equivalent representations of fractions in order to make comparisons

elaborations.name: VC2M6N03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing fractions on the same number line, paying attention to relative position, and using this to explain relationships between denominators

elaborations.name: VC2M6N03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining equivalence and order between fractions using number lines, drawings and models

elaborations.name: VC2M6N03-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and ordering fractions by placing cards on a string line across the room and referring to benchmark fractions to justify their position; for example, $\frac{5}{8}$ is greater than $\frac{1}{2}$ can be written as $\frac{5}{8}$ > $\frac{1}{2}$, because half of 8 is 4; $\frac{1}{6}$ is less than $\frac{1}{4}$, because 6 > 4 and can be written as $\frac{1}{6}$ < $\frac{1}{4}$

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N05 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions using knowledge of equivalent fractions

elaborations.name: VC2M6N05-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing addition and subtraction of fractions, using an understanding of equivalent fractions and methods such as jumps on a number line, or diagrams of fractions as parts of shapes

elaborations.name: VC2M6N05-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: determining the lowest common denominator using an understanding of prime and composite numbers to find equivalent representation of fractions when solving addition and subtraction problems

elaborations.name: VC2M6N05-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: calculating the addition or subtraction of fractions in the context of real-world problems (for example, using part cups or spoons in a recipe), using the understanding of equivalent fractions

elaborations.name: VC2M6N05-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the processes for adding and subtracting fractions with related denominators and fractions as an operator, in preparation for calculating with all fractions; for example, using fraction overlays and number lines to give meaning to adding and subtracting fractions with related and unrelated denominators

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E04
as_extracts.description: They use all 4 operations with decimals and connect decimal representations of measurements to the metric system.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N04 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: apply knowledge of place value to add and subtract decimals, using digital tools where appropriate; use estimation and rounding to check the reasonableness of answers

elaborations.name: VC2M6N04-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying estimation strategies to addition and subtraction of decimals to at least thousandths before calculating answers or when a situation requires just an estimation

elaborations.name: VC2M6N04-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying whole-number strategies; for example, using basic facts, place value, partitioning and the inverse relationship between addition and subtraction, and properties of operations to develop meaningful mental strategies for addition and subtraction of decimal numbers to at least hundredths

elaborations.name: VC2M6N04-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: working additively with linear measurements expressed as decimals up to 2 and 3 decimal places; for example, calculating how far off the world record the athletes were at the last Olympic Games in the women’s long jump or shot-put and comparing school records to the Olympic records

elaborations.name: VC2M6N04-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: deciding to use a calculator as a calculation strategy for solving additive problems involving decimals that vary in their number of decimal places beyond hundredths; for example, 1.0 − 0.0035 or 2.345 + 1.4999

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N06 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: multiply and divide decimals by multiples of powers of 10 without a calculator, applying knowledge of place value and proficiency with multiplication facts, using estimation and rounding to check the reasonableness of answers

elaborations.name: VC2M6N06-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying place value knowledge, including that the value of the digit is 10 times smaller each time a place is moved to the right, and known multiplication facts, to multiply and divide a decimal by powers of 10

elaborations.name: VC2M6N06-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying and explaining estimation strategies in multiplicative situations involving a decimal greater than one that is multiplied by a two- or three-digit number, using a multiple of 10 or 100 when the situation requires just an estimation

elaborations.name: VC2M6N06-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the effect of multiplying or dividing a decimal by 10, 100, 1000 … in terms of place value and not the decimal point shifting

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E05
as_extracts.description: Students solve problems involving finding a fraction, decimal or percentage of a quantity and use estimation to find approximate solutions to problems involving rational numbers and percentages.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N07 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: solve problems that require finding a familiar fraction, decimal or percentage of a quantity, including percentage discounts, choosing efficient calculation strategies with and without digital tools

elaborations.name: VC2M6N07-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining how $\frac{1}{3}$ of a quantity can be achieved by dividing by 3, and how knowledge of $\frac{1}{3}$ of a quantity can be used to find $\frac{2}{3}$ or $\frac{4}{3}$ of the same quantity, using situations involving money, length, duration, mass or capacity

elaborations.name: VC2M6N07-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating percentage discounts of 10%, 25% and 50% in an online toy sale, using their equivalent decimal representations of 0.10, 0.25 and 0.50 to calculate the amount of discount on sale items, with and without digital tools

elaborations.name: VC2M6N07-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: linking percentages to their decimal equivalent of tenths and hundredths and using these to determine percentage discounts; for example, finding a 30% discount by using its equivalence to 0.3, dividing by 10 and multiplying the result by 3 to give 30%

elaborations.name: VC2M6N07-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the equivalence between percentages and fractions, for example, $33\frac{1}{3}$% and $\frac{1}{3}$, keeping to percentages that are equivalent to fractions with small denominators such as 66$\frac{2}{3}$% and 12.5%

elaborations.name: VC2M6N07-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing a situation with a mathematical expression, for example, numbers and symbols such as $\frac{1}{4}$ × 24, that involves finding a familiar fraction or percentage of a quantity; and using mental strategies or a calculator and explaining the result in terms of the situation in question

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N08 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: approximate numerical solutions to problems involving rational numbers and percentages, using appropriate estimation strategies

elaborations.name: VC2M6N08-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using familiar fractions, decimals and percentages to approximate calculations, such as 0.3 of 180 is about $\frac{1}{3}$ of 180, or 52% is about $\frac{1}{2}$

elaborations.name: VC2M6N08-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing appropriate estimation strategies including rounding to the nearest whole number, knowledge of multiples of 2, 5 or 10 and partitioning numbers, in contexts such as measuring or cost per unit

elaborations.name: VC2M6N08-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the effect of rounding on calculations involving fractions or decimals and saying what numbers the answer will be between

elaborations.name: VC2M6N08-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the usefulness of estimation to check calculations for contexts such as dividing wood into a number of lengths, calculating cost per unit, reducing a recipe or dividing the cost of dinner for a group into individual amounts

elaborations.name: VC2M6N08-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: verifying solutions by estimating percentages in suitable contexts, such as discounts, using common percentages of 10%, 25%, 30%, 50% and 1%

elaborations.name: VC2M6N08-E06 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating estimation strategies to make decisions about steam cooking in ground ovens by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Peoples, including catering for different numbers of people and resources needed for cooking

as_extracts.description: They use mathematical modelling to solve financial and other practical problems involving percentages and rational numbers, formulating and solving the problem, and justifying choices.

content_descriptions.text: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving rational numbers and percentages, including in financial contexts; formulate the problems, choosing operations and using efficient mental and written calculation strategies, and using digital tools where appropriate; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, justifying the choices made

elaborations.name: VC2M6N09-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: modelling practical situations involving percentages using efficient calculation strategies to find solutions, such as mental calculations, spreadsheets, calculators or a variety of informal jottings, and interpreting the results in terms of the situation, for example, purchasing items during a sale

elaborations.name: VC2M6N09-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: modelling situations involving earning money and budgeting, asking questions such as ‘Can I afford it?’, ‘Do I need it?’ and ‘How much do I need to save for it?’ and developing a savings plan or budget for an upcoming event or personal purchase

elaborations.name: VC2M6N09-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: modelling and solving the problem of creating a budget for a class excursion or family holiday, using the internet to research costs and expenses, and representing the budget in a spreadsheet, creating and using formulas to calculate totals

as_extracts.description: Students find unknown values in numerical equations involving combinations of arithmetic operations.

content_descriptions.text: find unknown values in numerical equations involving brackets and combinations of arithmetic operations, using the properties of numbers and operations

elaborations.name: VC2M6A02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using brackets and the order of operations to write number sentences and appreciating the need for an agreed set of rules to complete multiple operations within the same number sentence; for example, for 40 ÷ 2 × (4 + 6) = □, you solve what is in the brackets first then complete the number sentence from left to right as there is no hierarchy between division and multiplication

elaborations.name: VC2M6A02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing equivalent number sentences involving brackets and combinations of the 4 operations, and explaining the need to have shared agreement on the order of operations when solving problems involving more than one operation to have unique solutions

elaborations.name: VC2M6A02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding pairs of unknown values in numerical equations that make the equation hold true; for example, listing possible combinations of natural numbers that make this statement true: 6 + 4 × 8 = 6 × Δ + □

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E08
as_extracts.description: They identify and explain rules used to create growing patterns.

content_descriptions.text: recognise and use rules that generate visually growing patterns and number patterns involving rational numbers

elaborations.name: VC2M6A01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating patterns such as the number of tiles in a geometric pattern, or the number of dots or other shapes in successive repeats of a strip or border pattern, looking for patterns in the way the numbers increase or decrease

elaborations.name: VC2M6A01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a calculator or spreadsheet to experiment with number patterns that result from multiplying or dividing; for example, 1 ÷ 9, 2 ÷ 9, 3 ÷ 9 …, 210 × 11, 211 × 11, 212 × 11 …, 111 × 11, 222 × 11, 333 × 11 …, or 100 ÷ 99, 101 ÷ 99, 102 ÷ 99 …

elaborations.name: VC2M6A01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating an extended number sequence that represents an additive pattern using decimals; for example, representing the additive pattern formed as students pay their $2.50 for an incursion as 2.50, 5.00, 7.50, 10.00, 12.50, 15.00, 17.50 …

elaborations.name: VC2M6A01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the number of regions created by successive folds of a sheet of paper (one fold, 2 regions; 2 folds, 4 regions; 3 folds, 8 regions) and describing the pattern using everyday language

elaborations.name: VC2M6A01-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a pattern sequence with materials, writing the associated number sequence and then describing the sequence with a rule so someone else can replicate it with different materials; for example, using matchsticks or toothpicks to create a growing pattern of triangles using 3 for one triangle, 5 for 2 triangles and 7 for 3 triangles and describing the pattern as ‘Multiply the number of triangles by 2 and then add one for the extra toothpick in the first triangle’

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E09
as_extracts.description: They design and use algorithms to generate sets of numbers, using a rule.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6A03 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: design and use algorithms involving a sequence of steps and decisions that use rules to generate sets of numbers; identify, interpret and explain emerging patterns

elaborations.name: VC2M6A03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an algorithm to create extended number sequences involving rational numbers, using a rule and digital tools, and explaining any emerging patterns

elaborations.name: VC2M6A03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing an algorithm to model operations, using the concept of input and output, describing and explaining relationships and any emerging patterns; for example, using function machines to model operations and recognising and comparing additive and multiplicative relationships

elaborations.name: VC2M6A03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing an algorithm or writing a simple program to generate a sequence of numbers based on the user’s input and a chosen operation, discussing any emerging patterns; for example, generating a sequence of numbers and comparing how quickly the sequences are growing in comparison to each other using the rule ‘add 2 to the input number’ compared to multiplying the input number by 2

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E10
as_extracts.description: Students interpret and use timetables, and measure, calculate and compare elapsed time.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6M03 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: measure, calculate and compare elapsed time; interpret and use timetables and itineraries to plan activities and determine the duration of events and journeys

elaborations.name: VC2M6M03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning a trip involving one or more modes of public transport

elaborations.name: VC2M6M03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing a timetable of daily activities for a planned event, for example, a sports carnival

elaborations.name: VC2M6M03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating different ways duration is represented in timetables and using different timetables to plan a journey

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E11
as_extracts.description: They convert between common units of length, mass and capacity.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6M01 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: convert between common metric units of length, mass and capacity; choose and use decimal representations of metric measurements relevant to the context of a problem

elaborations.name: VC2M6M01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the significance of the prefixes in units of measurement

elaborations.name: VC2M6M01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and using the correct operations when converting between units including millimetres, centimetres, metres, kilometres, milligrams, grams, kilograms, tonnes, millilitres, litres, kilolitres and megalitres

elaborations.name: VC2M6M01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the equivalence of measurements, such as 1.25 metres is the same as 125 centimetres

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E12
as_extracts.description: They use the formula for the area of a rectangle and angle properties to solve problems.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6M02 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: establish the formula for the area of a rectangle and use it to solve practical problems

elaborations.name: VC2M6M02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the relationship between the length and area of square units and the array structure to derive a formula for calculating the area of a rectangle from the lengths of its sides

elaborations.name: VC2M6M02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using one-centimetre grid paper to construct a variety of rectangles, recording the side lengths and the related areas of the rectangles in a table to establish the formula for the area of a rectangle by recognising the relationship between the length of the sides and its calculated area

elaborations.name: VC2M6M02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: solving problems involving the comparison of lengths and areas using appropriate units

elaborations.name: VC2M6M02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the connection between the perimeters of different rectangles with the same area and between the areas of rectangles with the same perimeter

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6M04 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: identify the relationships between angles on a straight line, angles at a point and vertically opposite angles; use these to determine unknown angles, communicating reasoning

elaborations.name: VC2M6M04-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using protractors or dynamic geometry software to measure and generalise about the size of angles formed when lines are crossed, and combinations of angles that meet at a point, including combinations that form right or straight angles

elaborations.name: VC2M6M04-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating the meaning of language associated with properties of angles, including right, complementary, complement, straight, supplement, vertically opposite, and angles at a point

elaborations.name: VC2M6M04-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the properties of supplementary and complementary angles to represent spatial situations with number sentences and solving to find the size of unknown angles

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E13
as_extracts.description: Students identify the parallel cross-section for right prisms.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6SP01 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: compare the parallel cross-sections of objects and recognise their relationships to right prisms

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using objects made of foam or polystyrene, slicing along different cross-sections, and recording the different shapes of faces that result; and comparing cross-sections of different objects

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using different pieces of fruit, slicing across different cross-sections, and drawing the cross-section; and reporting back to the class the results of the investigation

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing and drawing the shapes resulting from different ways of slicing through familiar objects; for example, slicing carrots at different angles or cutting through playdough models of objects; or using playdough models, fruit or similar to establish which objects can be cut in such a way that the cross-section will always be the same shape

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that right prisms are objects where parallel cross-sections perpendicular to the base of the prism are the same shape and size

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP01-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting different right prisms to the shape of their parallel cross-sections, such as a triangular prism, which can be described as a stack of the same-sized triangles, and a cube or square prism, which can be described as a stack of the same-sized squares

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP01-E06 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the design of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ dwellings, exploring the relationship between the cross-sections and the dwellings’ construction

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E14
as_extracts.description: They create tessellating patterns using combinations of transformations.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6SP03 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: recognise and use combinations of transformations to create tessellations and other geometric patterns, using dynamic geometry software where appropriate

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using digital tools to create tessellations of shapes, including paver and tiling patterns, describing the transformations used and discussing why these shapes tessellate; and identifying shapes or combinations of shapes that will or will not tessellate, answering questions such as ‘Do all triangles tessellate?’

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing a school or brand logo using the transformation of one or more shapes and describing the transformations used

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using dynamic geometry software and digital tools to experiment with transformations, for example, to demonstrate when the order of transformations produces different results; and experimenting with transformations and their application to fractals

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP03-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing an algorithm as a set of instructions to transform a shape, including getting back to where you started from; for example, programming a robot to move around the plane using instructions for movements, such as 2 down, 3 to the right, and combinations of these to transform shapes

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP03-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating symmetry, transformation and tessellation in different shapes on Country/Place, including rock formations, insects, and land and sea animals, discussing the purpose or role symmetry plays in their physical structure

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E15
as_extracts.description: They locate an ordered pair in any one of the 4 quadrants on the Cartesian plane.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6SP02 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: locate points in the 4 quadrants of the Cartesian plane; describe changes to the coordinates when a point is moved to a different position in the plane

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the Cartesian plane provides a graphical or visual way of describing location with respect to a fixed origin

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the axes are number lines that can have different scales, including fractions and decimals, depending on purpose

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the horizontal coordinate is written first and is changed if there is a move to the left or right, whereas a move up or down will change the vertical coordinate

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the Cartesian plane to draw lines and polygons, listing coordinates in the correct order to complete a polygon

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP02-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating and connecting land or star maps used by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples with the Cartesian plane through a graphical or visual way of describing location

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E16
as_extracts.description: Students compare distributions of discrete and continuous numerical and ordinal categorical data sets as part of their statistical investigations, using digital tools.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6ST01 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: interpret and compare data sets for ordinal and nominal categorical, discrete and continuous numerical variables using comparative displays or visualisations and digital tools; compare distributions in terms of mode, range and shape

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: determining the range for a numerical data set by finding the difference between the highest and the lowest value in the set and comparing the range for different data sets

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing acquired numerical data sets using side-by-side column graphs, comparing the spread of each data set using the range, the highest frequency for each data set using the mode, and discussing the shape

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing ordinal data collected through surveys, using visualisation tools including dot plots and bar charts, and discussing the distribution of data in terms of shape

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using technology to access data sets and graphing software to construct side-by-side column graphs or stacked line graphs; and comparing data sets that are grouped by gender, year level, age group or other variables, and discussing findings

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6ST03 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: plan and conduct statistical investigations by posing and refining questions to collect categorical or numerical data by observation or survey, or identifying a problem and collecting relevant data; analyse and interpret the data and communicate findings within the context of the investigation

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: selecting and using appropriate peripherals; for example, using a scientific probe to collect data about changing soil moisture for plants, interpreting the data and sharing the results as a digital chart

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a spreadsheet to record and analyse data, recognising the difference between cell formats in spreadsheets; for example, changing the default general format to numerical, text or date as needed

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the daily water usage by a student in the home compared to the World Health Organization claim that between 50 and 100 litres of clean water is needed per person per day

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST03-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting sample sets of ‘discrete numerical data’ (for example, the number of cars or pets in a household), where the class is surveyed, then other classes are surveyed, and data is analysed and compared, discussing findings

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST03-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting ordinal categorical data through the use of a survey; for example, surveying each member of the class, by asking them to indicate their preference on a five-point scale for a particular graphic and colour combination of a proposed school logo

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST03-E06 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: collecting ordinal data for ranking nominees for school captain with respect to several criteria, contrasting the use of a five-point scale compared with using a four-point scale

as_extracts.name: MAT6-E17
as_extracts.description: They critique arguments presented in the media based on statistics.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6ST02 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: identify statistically informed arguments presented in traditional and digital media; discuss and critique methods, data representations and conclusions

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating data representations in the media and discussing what they illustrate and the messages the people who created them might want to convey

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating reports and secondary data relating to the distribution and use of non-renewable resources around the world

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying potentially misleading data representations in the media; for example, graphs with broken axes or non-linear scales, graphics not drawn to scale, data not related to the population about which the claims are made and pie charts in which the whole pie does not represent the entire population about which the claims are made

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating both traditional and digital media relating to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, identifying and critiquing statistically informed arguments

as_extracts.description: Students assign probabilities using common fractions, decimals and percentages.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6P01 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: describe probabilities using fractions, decimals and percentages; recognise that probabilities lie on numerical scales of 0–1 or 0%–100%; use estimation to assign probabilities that events occur in a given context, using common fractions, percentages and decimals

elaborations.name: VC2M6P01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that the probability of an event occurring can be represented numerically as either a number ranging from zero to one or a percentage from 0% to 100% where zero or 0% means it will not happen and one or 100% means it is certain to happen

elaborations.name: VC2M6P01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a scale of zero to one or 0% to 100% to estimate chances of events

elaborations.name: VC2M6P01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: listing the different possible outcomes for rolling a dice and using a scale to locate the relative probability by considering the chance of more than or less than for each possible event, for example, the probability of getting a number greater than 4

elaborations.name: VC2M6P01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the language used to describe situations involving uncertainty, such as what it means to be ‘lucky’, a ‘75% chance’ of rain or a ‘1-in-100 years’ flood

elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children’s instructive games, such as Weme from the Warlpiri Peoples of Central Australia, to investigate and assign probabilities that events will occur, indicating their estimated likelihood
