as_extracts.name: MAT6-E19
as_extracts.description: They conduct simulations using digital tools, to generate and record the outcomes from many trials of a chance experiment. They compare observed frequencies to the expected frequencies of the outcomes of chance experiments.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M6P02 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: conduct repeated chance experiments and run simulations with an increasing number of trials using digital tools; compare observations with expected results and discuss the effect on variation of increasing the number of trials

elaborations.name: VC2M6P02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using digital tools to simulate multiple tosses of a coin or dice and comparing the relative frequency of an outcome as the number of trials increases; and identifying the variation between trials and realising that the results tend to the prediction with larger numbers of trials

elaborations.name: VC2M6P02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using online simulations of repeated random events to recognise emerging patterns, discussing and comparing expected results to the actual results

elaborations.name: VC2M6P02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the relative frequencies of all outcomes for a chance experiment and verifying that their sum equals one

elaborations.name: VC2M6P02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: systematically recording the outcome of large numbers of spins on a spinner and analysing the relative frequencies of outcomes, representing these as percentages

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N01 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: recognise situations, including financial contexts, that use integers; locate and represent integers on a number line and as coordinates on the Cartesian plane

elaborations.name: VC2M6N01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: extending the number line in the negative direction to locate and represent integers, recognising the difference in location between (−2) and (+2) and their relationship to zero as −2 < 0 < 2

elaborations.name: VC2M6N01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using integers to represent quantities in financial contexts, including the concept of profit and loss for a planned event

elaborations.name: VC2M6N01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using horizontal and vertical number lines to represent and find solutions to everyday problems involving locating and ordering integers around zero (for example, elevators, above and below sea level) and distinguishing a location by referencing the 4 quadrants of the Cartesian plane

elaborations.name: VC2M6N01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that the sign (positive or negative) indicates a direction in relation to zero – for example, 30 metres left of the admin block is (−30) and 20 metres right of the admin block is (+20) – and programming robots to move along a number line that is either horizontal or vertical but not both at the same time

elaborations.name: VC2M6N01-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing the temperatures of the different planets in the solar system, using a diagram of a thermometer that models a vertical number line

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N02 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: identify and describe the properties of prime, composite, square and triangular numbers and use these properties to solve problems and simplify calculations

elaborations.name: VC2M6N02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the definition of a prime number to explain why one is not a prime number

elaborations.name: VC2M6N02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: testing numbers by using division to distinguish between prime and composite numbers, recording the results on a number chart to identify any patterns

elaborations.name: VC2M6N02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing composite numbers as a product of their factors, including prime factors when necessary and using this form to simplify calculations involving multiplication, such as 15 × 16 as 5 × 3 × 4 × 4, which can be rearranged to simplify calculation to 5 × 4 × 3 × 4 = 20 × 12

elaborations.name: VC2M6N02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and describing the product of a number with itself as square; for example, 3 × 3 is the same as $3^{2}$

elaborations.name: VC2M6N02-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using spreadsheets to list all the numbers that have up to 3 factors, using combinations of only the first 3 prime numbers, recognising any emerging patterns, making conjectures and experimenting with other combinations

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N03 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: apply knowledge of equivalence to compare, order and represent common fractions, including halves, thirds and quarters, on the same number line and justify their order

elaborations.name: VC2M6N03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying factors and multiples to fraction denominators (such as halves with quarters, eighths and twelfths, and thirds with sixths, ninths and twelfths) to determine equivalent representations of fractions in order to make comparisons

elaborations.name: VC2M6N03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing fractions on the same number line, paying attention to relative position, and using this to explain relationships between denominators

elaborations.name: VC2M6N03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining equivalence and order between fractions using number lines, drawings and models

elaborations.name: VC2M6N03-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing and ordering fractions by placing cards on a string line across the room and referring to benchmark fractions to justify their position; for example, $\frac{5}{8}$ is greater than $\frac{1}{2}$ can be written as $\frac{5}{8}$ > $\frac{1}{2}$, because half of 8 is 4; $\frac{1}{6}$ is less than $\frac{1}{4}$, because 6 > 4 and can be written as $\frac{1}{6}$ < $\frac{1}{4}$

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N04 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: apply knowledge of place value to add and subtract decimals, using digital tools where appropriate; use estimation and rounding to check the reasonableness of answers

elaborations.name: VC2M6N04-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying estimation strategies to addition and subtraction of decimals to at least thousandths before calculating answers or when a situation requires just an estimation

elaborations.name: VC2M6N04-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying whole-number strategies; for example, using basic facts, place value, partitioning and the inverse relationship between addition and subtraction, and properties of operations to develop meaningful mental strategies for addition and subtraction of decimal numbers to at least hundredths

elaborations.name: VC2M6N04-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: working additively with linear measurements expressed as decimals up to 2 and 3 decimal places; for example, calculating how far off the world record the athletes were at the last Olympic Games in the women’s long jump or shot-put and comparing school records to the Olympic records

elaborations.name: VC2M6N04-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: deciding to use a calculator as a calculation strategy for solving additive problems involving decimals that vary in their number of decimal places beyond hundredths; for example, 1.0 − 0.0035 or 2.345 + 1.4999

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N05 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions using knowledge of equivalent fractions

elaborations.name: VC2M6N05-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing addition and subtraction of fractions, using an understanding of equivalent fractions and methods such as jumps on a number line, or diagrams of fractions as parts of shapes

elaborations.name: VC2M6N05-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: determining the lowest common denominator using an understanding of prime and composite numbers to find equivalent representation of fractions when solving addition and subtraction problems

elaborations.name: VC2M6N05-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: calculating the addition or subtraction of fractions in the context of real-world problems (for example, using part cups or spoons in a recipe), using the understanding of equivalent fractions

elaborations.name: VC2M6N05-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding the processes for adding and subtracting fractions with related denominators and fractions as an operator, in preparation for calculating with all fractions; for example, using fraction overlays and number lines to give meaning to adding and subtracting fractions with related and unrelated denominators

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N06 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: multiply and divide decimals by multiples of powers of 10 without a calculator, applying knowledge of place value and proficiency with multiplication facts, using estimation and rounding to check the reasonableness of answers

elaborations.name: VC2M6N06-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying place value knowledge, including that the value of the digit is 10 times smaller each time a place is moved to the right, and known multiplication facts, to multiply and divide a decimal by powers of 10

elaborations.name: VC2M6N06-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying and explaining estimation strategies in multiplicative situations involving a decimal greater than one that is multiplied by a two- or three-digit number, using a multiple of 10 or 100 when the situation requires just an estimation

elaborations.name: VC2M6N06-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the effect of multiplying or dividing a decimal by 10, 100, 1000 … in terms of place value and not the decimal point shifting

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N07 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: solve problems that require finding a familiar fraction, decimal or percentage of a quantity, including percentage discounts, choosing efficient calculation strategies with and without digital tools

elaborations.name: VC2M6N07-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining how $\frac{1}{3}$ of a quantity can be achieved by dividing by 3, and how knowledge of $\frac{1}{3}$ of a quantity can be used to find $\frac{2}{3}$ or $\frac{4}{3}$ of the same quantity, using situations involving money, length, duration, mass or capacity

elaborations.name: VC2M6N07-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating percentage discounts of 10%, 25% and 50% in an online toy sale, using their equivalent decimal representations of 0.10, 0.25 and 0.50 to calculate the amount of discount on sale items, with and without digital tools

elaborations.name: VC2M6N07-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: linking percentages to their decimal equivalent of tenths and hundredths and using these to determine percentage discounts; for example, finding a 30% discount by using its equivalence to 0.3, dividing by 10 and multiplying the result by 3 to give 30%

elaborations.name: VC2M6N07-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: explaining the equivalence between percentages and fractions, for example, $33\frac{1}{3}$% and $\frac{1}{3}$, keeping to percentages that are equivalent to fractions with small denominators such as 66$\frac{2}{3}$% and 12.5%

elaborations.name: VC2M6N07-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing a situation with a mathematical expression, for example, numbers and symbols such as $\frac{1}{4}$ × 24, that involves finding a familiar fraction or percentage of a quantity; and using mental strategies or a calculator and explaining the result in terms of the situation in question

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N08 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: approximate numerical solutions to problems involving rational numbers and percentages, using appropriate estimation strategies

elaborations.name: VC2M6N08-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using familiar fractions, decimals and percentages to approximate calculations, such as 0.3 of 180 is about $\frac{1}{3}$ of 180, or 52% is about $\frac{1}{2}$

elaborations.name: VC2M6N08-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing appropriate estimation strategies including rounding to the nearest whole number, knowledge of multiples of 2, 5 or 10 and partitioning numbers, in contexts such as measuring or cost per unit

elaborations.name: VC2M6N08-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the effect of rounding on calculations involving fractions or decimals and saying what numbers the answer will be between

elaborations.name: VC2M6N08-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the usefulness of estimation to check calculations for contexts such as dividing wood into a number of lengths, calculating cost per unit, reducing a recipe or dividing the cost of dinner for a group into individual amounts

elaborations.name: VC2M6N08-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: verifying solutions by estimating percentages in suitable contexts, such as discounts, using common percentages of 10%, 25%, 30%, 50% and 1%

elaborations.name: VC2M6N08-E06 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating estimation strategies to make decisions about steam cooking in ground ovens by Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Peoples, including catering for different numbers of people and resources needed for cooking

organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6N09 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving rational numbers and percentages, including in financial contexts; formulate the problems, choosing operations and using efficient mental and written calculation strategies, and using digital tools where appropriate; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, justifying the choices made

elaborations.name: VC2M6N09-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: modelling practical situations involving percentages using efficient calculation strategies to find solutions, such as mental calculations, spreadsheets, calculators or a variety of informal jottings, and interpreting the results in terms of the situation, for example, purchasing items during a sale

elaborations.name: VC2M6N09-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: modelling situations involving earning money and budgeting, asking questions such as ‘Can I afford it?’, ‘Do I need it?’ and ‘How much do I need to save for it?’ and developing a savings plan or budget for an upcoming event or personal purchase

elaborations.name: VC2M6N09-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: modelling and solving the problem of creating a budget for a class excursion or family holiday, using the internet to research costs and expenses, and representing the budget in a spreadsheet, creating and using formulas to calculate totals

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6A01 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use rules that generate visually growing patterns and number patterns involving rational numbers

elaborations.name: VC2M6A01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating patterns such as the number of tiles in a geometric pattern, or the number of dots or other shapes in successive repeats of a strip or border pattern, looking for patterns in the way the numbers increase or decrease

elaborations.name: VC2M6A01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using a calculator or spreadsheet to experiment with number patterns that result from multiplying or dividing; for example, 1 ÷ 9, 2 ÷ 9, 3 ÷ 9 …, 210 × 11, 211 × 11, 212 × 11 …, 111 × 11, 222 × 11, 333 × 11 …, or 100 ÷ 99, 101 ÷ 99, 102 ÷ 99 …

elaborations.name: VC2M6A01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating an extended number sequence that represents an additive pattern using decimals; for example, representing the additive pattern formed as students pay their $2.50 for an incursion as 2.50, 5.00, 7.50, 10.00, 12.50, 15.00, 17.50 …

elaborations.name: VC2M6A01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the number of regions created by successive folds of a sheet of paper (one fold, 2 regions; 2 folds, 4 regions; 3 folds, 8 regions) and describing the pattern using everyday language

elaborations.name: VC2M6A01-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a pattern sequence with materials, writing the associated number sequence and then describing the sequence with a rule so someone else can replicate it with different materials; for example, using matchsticks or toothpicks to create a growing pattern of triangles using 3 for one triangle, 5 for 2 triangles and 7 for 3 triangles and describing the pattern as ‘Multiply the number of triangles by 2 and then add one for the extra toothpick in the first triangle’

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6A02 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: find unknown values in numerical equations involving brackets and combinations of arithmetic operations, using the properties of numbers and operations

elaborations.name: VC2M6A02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using brackets and the order of operations to write number sentences and appreciating the need for an agreed set of rules to complete multiple operations within the same number sentence; for example, for 40 ÷ 2 × (4 + 6) = □, you solve what is in the brackets first then complete the number sentence from left to right as there is no hierarchy between division and multiplication

elaborations.name: VC2M6A02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing equivalent number sentences involving brackets and combinations of the 4 operations, and explaining the need to have shared agreement on the order of operations when solving problems involving more than one operation to have unique solutions

elaborations.name: VC2M6A02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding pairs of unknown values in numerical equations that make the equation hold true; for example, listing possible combinations of natural numbers that make this statement true: 6 + 4 × 8 = 6 × Δ + □

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6A03 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: design and use algorithms involving a sequence of steps and decisions that use rules to generate sets of numbers; identify, interpret and explain emerging patterns

elaborations.name: VC2M6A03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using an algorithm to create extended number sequences involving rational numbers, using a rule and digital tools, and explaining any emerging patterns

elaborations.name: VC2M6A03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing an algorithm to model operations, using the concept of input and output, describing and explaining relationships and any emerging patterns; for example, using function machines to model operations and recognising and comparing additive and multiplicative relationships

elaborations.name: VC2M6A03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing an algorithm or writing a simple program to generate a sequence of numbers based on the user’s input and a chosen operation, discussing any emerging patterns; for example, generating a sequence of numbers and comparing how quickly the sequences are growing in comparison to each other using the rule ‘add 2 to the input number’ compared to multiplying the input number by 2

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6M01 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: convert between common metric units of length, mass and capacity; choose and use decimal representations of metric measurements relevant to the context of a problem

elaborations.name: VC2M6M01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the significance of the prefixes in units of measurement

elaborations.name: VC2M6M01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying and using the correct operations when converting between units including millimetres, centimetres, metres, kilometres, milligrams, grams, kilograms, tonnes, millilitres, litres, kilolitres and megalitres

elaborations.name: VC2M6M01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the equivalence of measurements, such as 1.25 metres is the same as 125 centimetres

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6M02 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: establish the formula for the area of a rectangle and use it to solve practical problems

elaborations.name: VC2M6M02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the relationship between the length and area of square units and the array structure to derive a formula for calculating the area of a rectangle from the lengths of its sides

elaborations.name: VC2M6M02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using one-centimetre grid paper to construct a variety of rectangles, recording the side lengths and the related areas of the rectangles in a table to establish the formula for the area of a rectangle by recognising the relationship between the length of the sides and its calculated area

elaborations.name: VC2M6M02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: solving problems involving the comparison of lengths and areas using appropriate units

elaborations.name: VC2M6M02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the connection between the perimeters of different rectangles with the same area and between the areas of rectangles with the same perimeter

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6M03 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: measure, calculate and compare elapsed time; interpret and use timetables and itineraries to plan activities and determine the duration of events and journeys

elaborations.name: VC2M6M03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: planning a trip involving one or more modes of public transport

elaborations.name: VC2M6M03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing a timetable of daily activities for a planned event, for example, a sports carnival

elaborations.name: VC2M6M03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating different ways duration is represented in timetables and using different timetables to plan a journey

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6M04 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: identify the relationships between angles on a straight line, angles at a point and vertically opposite angles; use these to determine unknown angles, communicating reasoning

elaborations.name: VC2M6M04-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using protractors or dynamic geometry software to measure and generalise about the size of angles formed when lines are crossed, and combinations of angles that meet at a point, including combinations that form right or straight angles

elaborations.name: VC2M6M04-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: demonstrating the meaning of language associated with properties of angles, including right, complementary, complement, straight, supplement, vertically opposite, and angles at a point

elaborations.name: VC2M6M04-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the properties of supplementary and complementary angles to represent spatial situations with number sentences and solving to find the size of unknown angles

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6SP01 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: compare the parallel cross-sections of objects and recognise their relationships to right prisms

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using objects made of foam or polystyrene, slicing along different cross-sections, and recording the different shapes of faces that result; and comparing cross-sections of different objects

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using different pieces of fruit, slicing across different cross-sections, and drawing the cross-section; and reporting back to the class the results of the investigation

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: observing and drawing the shapes resulting from different ways of slicing through familiar objects; for example, slicing carrots at different angles or cutting through playdough models of objects; or using playdough models, fruit or similar to establish which objects can be cut in such a way that the cross-section will always be the same shape

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that right prisms are objects where parallel cross-sections perpendicular to the base of the prism are the same shape and size

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP01-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting different right prisms to the shape of their parallel cross-sections, such as a triangular prism, which can be described as a stack of the same-sized triangles, and a cube or square prism, which can be described as a stack of the same-sized squares

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP01-E06 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the design of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ dwellings, exploring the relationship between the cross-sections and the dwellings’ construction

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6SP02 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: locate points in the 4 quadrants of the Cartesian plane; describe changes to the coordinates when a point is moved to a different position in the plane

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the Cartesian plane provides a graphical or visual way of describing location with respect to a fixed origin

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the axes are number lines that can have different scales, including fractions and decimals, depending on purpose

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that the horizontal coordinate is written first and is changed if there is a move to the left or right, whereas a move up or down will change the vertical coordinate

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the Cartesian plane to draw lines and polygons, listing coordinates in the correct order to complete a polygon

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP02-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating and connecting land or star maps used by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples with the Cartesian plane through a graphical or visual way of describing location

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6SP03 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use combinations of transformations to create tessellations and other geometric patterns, using dynamic geometry software where appropriate

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using digital tools to create tessellations of shapes, including paver and tiling patterns, describing the transformations used and discussing why these shapes tessellate; and identifying shapes or combinations of shapes that will or will not tessellate, answering questions such as ‘Do all triangles tessellate?’

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing a school or brand logo using the transformation of one or more shapes and describing the transformations used

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using dynamic geometry software and digital tools to experiment with transformations, for example, to demonstrate when the order of transformations produces different results; and experimenting with transformations and their application to fractals

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP03-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: designing an algorithm as a set of instructions to transform a shape, including getting back to where you started from; for example, programming a robot to move around the plane using instructions for movements, such as 2 down, 3 to the right, and combinations of these to transform shapes

elaborations.name: VC2M6SP03-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating symmetry, transformation and tessellation in different shapes on Country/Place, including rock formations, insects, and land and sea animals, discussing the purpose or role symmetry plays in their physical structure

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6ST01 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: interpret and compare data sets for ordinal and nominal categorical, discrete and continuous numerical variables using comparative displays or visualisations and digital tools; compare distributions in terms of mode, range and shape

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: determining the range for a numerical data set by finding the difference between the highest and the lowest value in the set and comparing the range for different data sets

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing acquired numerical data sets using side-by-side column graphs, comparing the spread of each data set using the range, the highest frequency for each data set using the mode, and discussing the shape

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing ordinal data collected through surveys, using visualisation tools including dot plots and bar charts, and discussing the distribution of data in terms of shape

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using technology to access data sets and graphing software to construct side-by-side column graphs or stacked line graphs; and comparing data sets that are grouped by gender, year level, age group or other variables, and discussing findings

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M6ST02 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: identify statistically informed arguments presented in traditional and digital media; discuss and critique methods, data representations and conclusions

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating data representations in the media and discussing what they illustrate and the messages the people who created them might want to convey

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: evaluating reports and secondary data relating to the distribution and use of non-renewable resources around the world

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying potentially misleading data representations in the media; for example, graphs with broken axes or non-linear scales, graphics not drawn to scale, data not related to the population about which the claims are made and pie charts in which the whole pie does not represent the entire population about which the claims are made

elaborations.name: VC2M6ST02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating both traditional and digital media relating to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, identifying and critiquing statistically informed arguments

curriculum_level_description.body:
In Level 7, learning in Mathematics builds on each student’s prior learning and experiences. Students engage in a range of approaches to the learning and doing of mathematics that develop their understanding of and fluency with concepts, procedures and processes by making connections, reasoning, problem-solving and practice. Proficiency in mathematics enables students to respond to familiar and unfamiliar situations by employing mathematical strategies to make informed decisions and solve problems efficiently.

Students further develop proficiency and positive dispositions towards mathematics and its use as they:

  • extend their understanding of the integer and rational number systems; strengthen their fluency with mental calculation, written algorithms and digital tools; and routinely consider the reasonableness of results in context
  • use exponents and exponent notation to consolidate and formalise their understanding of representations of natural numbers, and use these to make conjectures involving natural numbers by experiment, with the assistance of digital tools
  • recognise, develop and use algebraic expressions and formulas using conventions, notations, symbols and pronumerals; and interpret algebraic expressions and formulas, use substitution to evaluate and determine unknown terms where other values are given, and solve simple equations using a variety of methods
  • use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving rational numbers, ratios and percentages, formulating and making choices about representations, calculation strategies and communicating solutions within the context
  • use variables, constants, relations and functions to express relationships in real-life data and interpret key features of their representation in rules, tables and graphs
  • extend their knowledge of angles to establish further relationships and apply these when solving measurement and spatial problems
  • create and use algorithms to classify shapes in the plane and use tools to construct shapes, including two-dimensional representations of prisms and other objects
  • use coordinates in the Cartesian plane to describe transformations
  • apply the statistical investigation process to obtain numerical data relating to questions of interest, choose displays for the distributions of data and interpret summary statistics for determining the centre and spread of the data in context
  • conduct probability simulations and experiments involving chance events, and construct corresponding sample spaces and observe related frequencies, comparing expected, simulated and experimental results.

curriculum_achievement_standard.body:
By the end of Level 7, students represent natural numbers in expanded form and as products of prime factors, using exponent notation. They solve problems involving squares of numbers and square roots of perfect square numbers. Students solve problems involving addition and subtraction of integers. They use all 4 operations in calculations involving positive fractions and decimals, choosing efficient mental and written calculation strategies. Students choose between equivalent representations of rational numbers and percentages to assist in calculations and make simple estimates to judge the reasonableness of results. They use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving rational numbers, percentages and ratios in spatial, financial and other applied contexts, justifying choices of representation.

Students use algebraic expressions to represent situations, describe the relationships between variables from authentic data and substitute values into formulas to determine unknown values. They solve linear equations with natural number solutions and verify their solutions through substitution. Students create tables of values relating to algebraic expressions and formulas, and describe how the values change.

Students apply knowledge of angle relationships and the sum of angles in a triangle to solve problems, giving reasons. They establish and use formulas for the areas of triangles and parallelograms and the volumes of rectangular and triangular prisms to solve problems. They describe the relationships between the radius, diameter and circumference of a circle.

Students classify polygons according to their features and design an algorithm to sort and classify shapes. They represent objects two-dimensionally in different ways, describing the usefulness of these representations. They use coordinates to describe transformations of points in the plane.

Students plan and conduct statistical investigations involving discrete and continuous numerical data, using appropriate displays. They interpret data in terms of the shape of distribution and summary statistics, identifying possible outliers. They decide which measure of central tendency is most suitable and explain their reasoning.

Students list sample spaces for single-step experiments, assign probabilities to outcomes of events and predict relative frequencies for related events. They conduct repeated single-step chance experiments and run simulations using digital tools, giving reasons for differences between predicted and observed results.

as_extracts.description: They solve linear equations with natural number solutions and verify their solutions through substitution.

elaborations.name: VC2M7A03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that solving an equation is a process of determining a value that makes the equation true; and using substitution to determine whether a given number is a solution to an equation or not

elaborations.name: VC2M7A03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: solving equations using concrete materials, the balance model and backtracking, explaining the process

elaborations.name: VC2M7A03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: solving linear equations such as $3x+7=19$ algebraically, and verifying the solution by substitution

as_extracts.description: Students create tables of values relating to algebraic expressions and formulas, and describe how the values change.

content_descriptions.text: generate tables of values from visually changing patterns or the rule of a function; describe and plot these relationships on the Cartesian plane

elaborations.name: VC2M7A05-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: plotting points from a table of values generated using simple linear functions and recognising patterns, such as the points lie on a straight line

elaborations.name: VC2M7A05-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing and using variables to create a general rule and using the rule to determine the value of the dependent variable for any given value of the independent variable; for example, plotting the value of the circumference of a circle for varying values of radius

elaborations.name: VC2M7A05-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using function machines to generate a table of ordered pairs using input and output values, plotting the relationships on a Cartesian plane and describing the graph in terms of shape

elaborations.name: VC2M7A05-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using diagrams and manipulatives to form linear growth patterns, representing these patterns in tables and describing the relationship in terms of the way the pattern is growing and in the context of the situation

content_descriptions.name: VC2M7A06 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: manipulate formulas involving several variables using digital tools, and describe the effect of systematic variation in the values of the variables

elaborations.name: VC2M7A06-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: experimenting with different sets of tables of values from formulas; for example, using volume of a rectangular prism = length × width × height, and specifying a fixed width and equal length and varying the height

elaborations.name: VC2M7A06-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using spreadsheets and the formula function to recognise the effect of changing parameters on the entries in cells

elaborations.name: VC2M7A06-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: analysing distance travelled for different combinations of average speed and time of travel using a table of values and the distance formula

content_descriptions.name: VC2M7M04 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: identify corresponding, alternate and co-interior relationships between angles formed when parallel lines are crossed by a transversal; use them to solve problems and explain reasons

elaborations.name: VC2M7M04-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing a pair of parallel lines and a pair of perpendicular lines using their properties, a pair of compasses and a ruler and set squares, or using dynamic geometry software

elaborations.name: VC2M7M04-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using dynamic geometry software to identify relationships between alternate, corresponding and co-interior angles for a pair of parallel lines cut by a transversal

elaborations.name: VC2M7M04-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using dynamic geometry software to demonstrate how angles and their properties are involved in the design and construction of scissor lifts, folding umbrellas, toolboxes and cherry pickers

elaborations.name: VC2M7M04-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using geometric reasoning of angle properties to generalise the angle relationships of parallel lines and transversals, and related properties, such as the size of an exterior angle of a triangle is equal to the sum of the sizes of opposite and non-adjacent interior angles, and the sum of the sizes of interior angles in a triangle in the plane is equal to the size of 2 right angles or 180°

content_descriptions.name: VC2M7M05 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: demonstrate that the interior angle sum of a triangle in the plane is 180° and apply this to determine the interior angle sum of other shapes and the size of unknown angles

elaborations.name: VC2M7M05-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using concrete materials to demonstrate that the sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180°; for example, using paper triangles and tearing to demonstrate that the interior angles when combined form 180°

elaborations.name: VC2M7M05-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using decomposition and the angle sum of a triangle to generalise the interior angle sum of an $𝑛$-sided polygon, as $180(n−2)=180n−360$

as_extracts.description: They establish and use formulas for the areas of triangles and parallelograms and the volumes of rectangular and triangular prisms to solve problems.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M7M01 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: establish the formulas for areas of rectangles, triangles and parallelograms and use these in problem-solving

elaborations.name: VC2M7M01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: building on the understanding of the area of rectangles to develop formulas for the area of triangles

elaborations.name: VC2M7M01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: establishing that the area of a triangle is half the area of an appropriate rectangle

elaborations.name: VC2M7M01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using area formulas for rectangles and triangles to solve problems involving areas of surfaces

content_descriptions.name: VC2M7M02 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: solve problems involving the volume of right prisms including rectangular and triangular prisms, using established formulas and appropriate units

elaborations.name: VC2M7M02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: building a rectangular prism out of unit cubes and showing that the measure of volume is the same as would be found by multiplying the 3 edge lengths or by multiplying the area of the base by the height/length

elaborations.name: VC2M7M02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing the connection between the area of the parallel cross-section (base), the height and the volume of a rectangular or triangular prism to other prisms

elaborations.name: VC2M7M02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting the area of the floor space and the number of floors of a high-rise building to calculate the volume of a building

elaborations.name: VC2M7M02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using dynamic geometry software, spatial reasoning and prediction to derive the formula for the volume of prisms

as_extracts.name: MAT7-E12
as_extracts.description: They describe the relationships between the radius, diameter and circumference of a circle.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M7M03 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: describe the relationship between $\pi$ and the circumference, radius and diameter of a circle

elaborations.name: VC2M7M03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the features of circles and their relationships to one another; for example, labelling the parts of a circle including centre, radius, diameter and circumference and using one of radius, diameter or circumference to determine the measure of the other 2; and understanding that the diameter of a circle is twice the radius, or that the radius is the circumference divided by $2\pi$

elaborations.name: VC2M7M03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the circumference of circles in relation to their radius and diameter with materials and measuring, to establish measurement formulas; for example, using a compass to draw several circles, then using string to approximate the circumference, comparing the length of string to the diameter of the circle

elaborations.name: VC2M7M03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating $\pi$ as the constant in the proportional relationship between the circumference of a circle and its diameter, and historical approximations from different civilisations, including Egypt, Babylon, Greece, India and China

elaborations.name: VC2M7M03-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the applications and significance of circles in everyday life of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, such as in basketry, symbols and architecture, recognising the relationships between the centre, radius, diameter and circumference

elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a classification scheme for triangles based on sides and angles, using a flow chart that uses sequences and decisions

elaborations.elaboration_text: creating a classification scheme for regular, irregular, concave or convex polygons that are sorted according to the number of sides

elaborations.elaboration_text: using aerial views of buildings and other three-dimensional structures to visualise the footprint made by the building or structure, identifying prisms that could approximate the structure

elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring different two-dimensional representations of objects in Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander artworks or cultural maps of Country/Place

elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the mean, median, mode and range of displays of data from a given context, and explaining how outliers may affect summary statistics

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how different data sets can have the same measures of central tendency and experimenting with how varying data affects these measures

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: acquiring continuous numerical data by taking measurement samples during a science experiment, observation or field study, comparing measures of central tendency and identifying any anomalies in the distribution of data

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using ordered stem-and-leaf plots to record and display numerical data collected in a class investigation, such as constructing a class plot of height in centimetres on a shared stem-and-leaf plot for which the stems 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 have been produced

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST02-E02 - Mathematics

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting features of the data display (for example, highest frequency, clusters, gaps, symmetry or skewness) to the mode, range and median, and the question in context; describing the shape of distributions using terms such as ‘positive skew’, ‘negative skew’, ‘symmetric’ and ‘bi-modal’ and discussing the location of the median and mean on these distributions

elaborations.elaboration_text: using mean and median to compare data sets, identifying possible outliers and explaining how these may affect the comparison; recognising how different displays make specific information about data more evident, including proportions, and measures of mean, mode or median, spread and extreme values; understanding that the median and the mean will be the same or similar for symmetric distributions but different for distributions that are skewed

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST02-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the mean and median of data with and without extremes; for example, estimation of standard measures for length or mass, informally considering for a given set of data what might constitute an unexpected, unusual or extreme data value

content_descriptions.text: acquire data sets for discrete and continuous numerical variables and calculate the range, median, mean and mode; make and justify decisions about which measures of central tendency provide useful insights into the nature of the distribution of data

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: understanding that summarising data by calculating measures of centre can help make sense of the data, commenting on skewness or symmetry of data and the use of mean and median as representative measures

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the mean, median, mode and range of displays of data from a given context, and explaining how outliers may affect summary statistics

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising how different data sets can have the same measures of central tendency and experimenting with how varying data affects these measures

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: acquiring continuous numerical data by taking measurement samples during a science experiment, observation or field study, comparing measures of central tendency and identifying any anomalies in the distribution of data

content_descriptions.name: VC2M7ST02 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: create different types of displays of numerical data, including dot plots and stem-and-leaf plots, using software where appropriate; describe and compare the distribution of data, commenting on the shape, centre and spread including outliers and determining the range, median, mean and mode

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using ordered stem-and-leaf plots to record and display numerical data collected in a class investigation, such as constructing a class plot of height in centimetres on a shared stem-and-leaf plot for which the stems 12, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 17 have been produced

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing variation in attributes by category using split stem-and-leaf plots or dot plots; interpreting the shape of the distribution using qualitative terms to describe ‘symmetry’, ‘skewness’ and ‘average’ in terms of the mean, median and mode, and the amount of variation based on qualitative descriptions of the spread of the data

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting features of the data display (for example, highest frequency, clusters, gaps, symmetry or skewness) to the mode, range and median, and the question in context; describing the shape of distributions using terms such as ‘positive skew’, ‘negative skew’, ‘symmetric’ and ‘bi-modal’ and discussing the location of the median and mean on these distributions

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using mean and median to compare data sets, identifying possible outliers and explaining how these may affect the comparison; recognising how different displays make specific information about data more evident, including proportions, and measures of mean, mode or median, spread and extreme values; understanding that the median and the mean will be the same or similar for symmetric distributions but different for distributions that are skewed

elaborations.name: VC2M7ST02-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the mean and median of data with and without extremes; for example, estimation of standard measures for length or mass, informally considering for a given set of data what might constitute an unexpected, unusual or extreme data value

as_extracts.name: MAT7-E18
as_extracts.description: Students list sample spaces for single-step experiments, assign probabilities to outcomes of events and predict relative frequencies for related events.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M7P01 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: identify the sample space for single-stage experiments; assign probabilities to the possible outcomes and predict relative frequencies for related experiments

elaborations.name: VC2M7P01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing the meaning of probability terminology, for example, ‘probability’, ‘sample space’, ‘favourable outcome’, ‘trial’, ‘experiment’ and ‘event’

elaborations.name: VC2M7P01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: listing sample spaces for games involving throwing a coin or a dice, spinners, or lucky dip

elaborations.name: VC2M7P01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: assigning the probability for throwing a 6 on a dice and using this to predict the number of times a 6 will occur when a dice is thrown multiple times

as_extracts.name: MAT7-E19
as_extracts.description: They conduct repeated single-step chance experiments and run simulations using digital tools, giving reasons for differences between predicted and observed results.

content_descriptions.name: VC2M7P02 - Mathematics
content_descriptions.text: conduct repeated chance experiments and run simulations with a large number of trials using digital tools; compare predicted with observed results, explaining the differences and the effect of sample size on the outcomes

elaborations.name: VC2M7P02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing an understanding of the law of large numbers through using experiments and simulations to conduct large numbers of trials for seemingly random events and discussing findings

elaborations.name: VC2M7P02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: conducting simulations using online simulation tools and comparing the combined results of a large number of trials to predicted results

elaborations.name: VC2M7P02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: exploring and observing Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children’s instructive games – for example, Koara from the Jawi and Bardi Peoples of Sunday Island in Western Australia – to investigate probability, predicting outcomes for an event and comparing with increasingly larger numbers of trials, and comparing observed and expected results

organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.

organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander societies are diverse and have distinct cultural expressions, such as language, customs and beliefs. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have the right to maintain, control, protect and develop their cultural expressions, while also maintaining the right to control, protect and develop culture as Indigenous Cultural and Intellectual Property.

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAC2
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ ways of life reflect unique ways of being, knowing, thinking and doing.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPAP1
organising_ideas.text: Australia has 2 distinct First Nations Peoples; each encompasses a diversity of nations across Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples have occupied the Australian continent and adjacent islands from time immemorial.
organising_ideas.ccp: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7N01 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: describe the relationship between perfect square numbers and square roots, and use squares of numbers and square roots of perfect square numbers to solve problems

elaborations.name: VC2M7N01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating squares of natural numbers from one to 20, and connecting them to visual representations such as dots arranged in a square pattern

elaborations.name: VC2M7N01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the square and square root notation, and the distributive property and area diagrams, to calculate the squares of two-digit numbers; for example, $43^{2}=(40+3)^{2}=40^{2}+2\times40\times3+3^{2}=1600+240+9=1849$

elaborations.name: VC2M7N01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: determining between which 2 consecutive natural numbers the square root of a given number lies; for example, 43 is between the square numbers 36 and 49 so $\sqrt{43}$ is between $\sqrt{36}$ and $\sqrt{49}$ and therefore between 6 and 7

elaborations.name: VC2M7N01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: generating a list of perfect square numbers and describing any emerging patterns, for example, the last digit of perfect square numbers, or the difference between consecutive square numbers, and recognising the constant second difference

elaborations.name: VC2M7N01-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using the relationship between perfect square numbers and their square roots to determine the perimeter of a square tiled floor using square tiles; for example, an area of floor with 144 square tiles has a perimeter of 48 tile lengths

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7N02 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: represent natural numbers in expanded notation using powers of 10, and as products of powers of prime numbers using exponent notation

elaborations.name: VC2M7N02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying and explaining the connections between place value and expanded notations, for example, $7000=7\times 10^{3}$ and $3750=3\times 10^{3}+7\times 10^{2}+5\times 10^{1}$

elaborations.name: VC2M7N02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying knowledge of factors to strategies for expressing natural numbers as products of powers of prime factors, such as repeated division by prime factors or creating factor trees, for example, $48=6\times 8=2\times 3\times 2\times 2\times 2=3^{1}\times 2^{4}=3\times 2^{4}$

elaborations.name: VC2M7N02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing familiarity with the sequence 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512 and powers of 2; the sequence 1, 3, 9, 27, 81, 243, 729 and powers of 3; and the sequence 1, 5, 25, 125, 625 and powers of 5

elaborations.name: VC2M7N02-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: solving problems involving lowest common multiples and greatest common divisors (highest common factors) for pairs of natural numbers by comparing their prime factorisation

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7N03 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: find equivalent representations of rational numbers and represent positive and negative rational numbers and mixed numbers on a number line

elaborations.name: VC2M7N03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating equivalence of fractions using common multiples and a fraction wall, diagrams or a number line to show that a fraction such as $\frac{2}{3}$ is equivalent to $\frac{4}{6}$ and $\frac{6}{9}$ and therefore $\frac{2}{3}$ < $\frac{5}{6}$

elaborations.name: VC2M7N03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: expressing a fraction in simplest form using common divisors

elaborations.name: VC2M7N03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying and explaining the equivalence between fraction, decimal and percentage representations of rational numbers, for example, 16%, 0.16, $\frac{16}{100}$ and $\frac{4}{25}$, using manipulatives, number lines or diagrams

elaborations.name: VC2M7N03-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: representing positive and negative fractions and mixed numerals on various intervals of the real number line, including intervals that are not symmetrical about zero

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7N04 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: round decimals to a given accuracy appropriate to the context and use appropriate rounding and estimation to check the reasonableness of computations

elaborations.name: VC2M7N04-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: identifying the interval between a pair of consecutive integers that includes a given rational number

elaborations.name: VC2M7N04-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing and applying conventions for rounding correct to a specified number of decimal places based upon the context

elaborations.name: VC2M7N04-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: checking that the accuracy of rounding is suitable for context and purpose; for example, for the amount of paint required or the cost estimate for renovating a house, purchasing 2 litres of paint to paint the bedroom even though 1.89 litres is the exact answer or estimating a renovation budget to the nearest $100

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7N05 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: multiply and divide fractions and decimals using efficient mental and written strategies, and digital tools

elaborations.name: VC2M7N05-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating multiplication of fractions and decimals, using strategies including patterning and multiplication as repeated addition, with both concrete materials and digital tools, and identifying the processes for division as the inverse of multiplication

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7N06 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: use the 4 operations with positive rational numbers, including fractions and decimals, to solve problems using efficient mental and written calculation strategies

elaborations.name: VC2M7N06-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: solving addition and subtraction problems involving fractions and decimals; for example, using rectangular arrays with dimensions equal to the denominators, algebra tiles, digital tools or informal jottings

elaborations.name: VC2M7N06-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: choosing an appropriate numerical representation for a problem so that efficient computations can be made, such as 12.5%, $\frac{1}{8}$, 0.125 or $\frac{125}{1000}$

elaborations.name: VC2M7N06-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing efficient strategies with appropriate use of the commutative and associative properties, place value, patterning, and multiplication facts to solve multiplication and division problems involving fractions and decimals; for example, using the commutative property to calculate $\frac{2}{3}$ of $\frac{1}{2}$, giving $\frac{1}{2}$ of $\frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{3}$

elaborations.name: VC2M7N06-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: solving multiplicative problems involving fractions and decimals using fraction walls, rectangular arrays, algebra tiles, calculators or informal jottings

elaborations.name: VC2M7N06-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing efficient strategies with appropriate use of the commutative and associative properties, regrouping or partitioning to solve additive problems involving fractions and decimals

elaborations.name: VC2M7N06-E06 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: carrying out calculations to solve problems using the representation that makes computations efficient, such as 12.5% of 96 is more efficiently calculated as $\frac{1}{8}$ of 96, including contexts such as comparing land use by calculating the total local municipal area set aside for parkland or manufacturing and retail, the amount of protein in daily food intake across several days, or increases or decreases in energy accounts each account cycle

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS2
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable patterns of living require the responsible use of resources; circular economies; maintenance of clean air, water and soils; and the restoration of healthy environments and habitats with ecological integrity.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSIS3
organising_ideas.text: Economic, social, environmental and cultural systems influence the sustainability of Earth’s systems.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSRD1
organising_ideas.text: Responsibly designed products and services aim to minimise the human impact on the environment and restore the quality, ecological integrity and diversity of economic, social, environmental and cultural systems.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSRD3
organising_ideas.text: Responsible design requires a recognition and appreciation of land custodianship, past practices, contemporary research and technological advancements, and balanced and informed decisions based on understanding possible interconnected economic, social, environmental and cultural impacts.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSFT1
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable futures thinking is based on informed views that consider possible and desirable futures. It leads to individual, community, organisational and political action that reduces risk.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

organising_ideas.name: Sustainability - VC2CCPSFT3
organising_ideas.text: Sustainable futures thinking requires individuals to think creatively, seek information, identify a variety of possibilities, reflect and evaluate actions, and collaborate with and influence others as they work towards desired futures.
organising_ideas.ccp: Sustainability

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7N07 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: find percentages of quantities and express one quantity as a percentage of another, with and without digital tools

elaborations.name: VC2M7N07-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using authentic problems to express quantities as percentages of other amounts

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7N08 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: compare, order and solve problems involving addition and subtraction of integers

elaborations.name: VC2M7N08-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using less-than and greater-than notation in expressions when comparing and ordering integers; for example, negative 5 is less than positive 2 and can be represented as $(-5)<(+2)$; $(-3)>(-6)$

elaborations.name: VC2M7N08-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: discussing language such as ‘addition’, ‘subtraction’, ‘magnitude’, ‘difference’ and ‘sign’ and synonyms of these terms

elaborations.name: VC2M7N08-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: ordering, adding and subtracting integers using a number line

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7N09 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: recognise, represent and solve problems involving ratios

elaborations.name: VC2M7N09-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using diagrams, physical or virtual materials to represent ratios, recognising that ratios express the quantitative relationship between 2 or more groups; for example, using counters or coloured beads to show the ratios 1:4 and 1:1:2

elaborations.name: VC2M7N09-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using fractions to solve ratio problems involving comparison of quantities and considering part-part and part-whole relations; for example, dividing a set into the ratio 1:2 by determining the number of parts as 3

elaborations.name: VC2M7N09-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: sharing quantities in a given ratio; for example, sharing an amount of money in a given ratio, such as sharing $20 in the ratio 2:3

elaborations.name: VC2M7N09-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: applying ratios to realistic and meaningful contexts – for example, mixing 500 millilitres of a liquid with a concentration of 1:4 means $\frac{1}{5}$ concentrate and $\frac{4}{5}$ water so, 0.2 of 500 millilitres is concentrate and 0.8 of 500 millilitres is water – and interpreting results in context

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7N10 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: use mathematical modelling to solve practical problems involving rational numbers and percentages, including financial contexts such as ‘best buys’; formulate problems, choosing representations and efficient calculation strategies, designing algorithms and using digital tools as appropriate; interpret and communicate solutions in terms of the situation, justifying choices made about the representation

elaborations.name: VC2M7N10-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: modelling additive situations involving positive and negative quantities; for example, a lift travelling up and down floors in a high-rise apartment where the ground floor is interpreted as zero, or in geography when determining altitude above and below sea level

elaborations.name: VC2M7N10-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: modelling contexts involving proportion, such as the proportion of students attending the school disco, proportion of the bottle cost to the recycling refund, proportion of the school site that is green space, 55% of Year 7 students attended the end of term function or 23% of the school population voted ‘yes’ to a change of school uniform; and interpreting and communicating answers in terms of the context of the situation

elaborations.name: VC2M7N10-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: modelling financial problems involving profit and loss, credits and debits, gains and losses; for example, holding a fundraising sausage sizzle and determining whether the event made a percentage profit or loss

elaborations.name: VC2M7N10-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: finding the sum of a set of consecutive numbers using a loop structure

elaborations.name: VC2M7N10-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: constructing geometric patterns such as a honeycomb, using dynamic geometry functionality

elaborations.name: VC2M7N10-E06 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using mathematical modelling to investigate the proportion of land mass/area of Aboriginal Peoples’ traditional grain belt compared with Australia’s current grain belt

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7A01 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: recognise and use variables to represent everyday formulas algebraically and substitute values into formulas to determine an unknown

elaborations.name: VC2M7A01-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: linking variables to attributes and measures being modelled when using formulas, such as the area of a rectangle is equal to the length × width as $A=l\times w$ or using $p=6g+b$ to describe a total of points expressed as goals (worth 6 points) and behinds (worth one point)

elaborations.name: VC2M7A01-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: interpreting and using formulas obtained from other sources, for example, maximum heart rates and target heart rates for moderate exercise

elaborations.name: VC2M7A01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: substituting numerical values for variables when using formulas and calculating the value of an unknown in practical situations; for example, calculating weekly wage $W$ given base wage $b$ and overtime hours $h$ at 1.5 times rate $r$, $W=b+1.5\times h\times r$, using values for mass $m$ and volume $v$ to determine density $d$ of a substance where $d=\frac{m}{v}$

elaborations.name: VC2M7A01-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using everyday formulas and their application to contexts on Country/Place, investigating the relationships between variables

organising_ideas.name: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Histories and Cultures - VC2CCPACP1
organising_ideas.text: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities of Australia maintain a deep connection to, and responsibility for, Country and Place and have holistic values and belief systems that are connected to the land, sea, sky and waterways.

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7A02 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: apply the associative, commutative and distributive laws to aid mental and written computation, and formulate algebraic expressions using constants, variables, operations and brackets

elaborations.name: VC2M7A02-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: simplifying calculations

elaborations.name: VC2M7A02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: forming simple estimates for calculations involving multiple and/or combined operations

elaborations.name: VC2M7A02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: generalising arithmetic expressions to algebraic expressions involving constants, variables, operations and brackets; for example, $7+7+7=3\times 7$, $x+x+x=3\times x$ noting that $3x$ includes implied multiplication and recognising the difference between $3x+4$ and $3(x+4)$

elaborations.name: VC2M7A02-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: formulating algebraic expressions that represent mathematical relationships; for example, translating from words to symbols in ‘think of a number’ type activities

elaborations.name: VC2M7A02-E05 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising and applying the concept of variable as something that can change in value, investigating the relationships between variables, and the application to processes on Country/Place, including how cultural expressions of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, such as storytelling, communicate mathematical relationships that can be represented as mathematical expressions

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7A03 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: solve one-variable linear equations of increasing complexity with natural number solutions; verify equation solutions by substitution

elaborations.name: VC2M7A03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising that solving an equation is a process of determining a value that makes the equation true; and using substitution to determine whether a given number is a solution to an equation or not

elaborations.name: VC2M7A03-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: solving equations using concrete materials, the balance model and backtracking, explaining the process

elaborations.name: VC2M7A03-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: solving linear equations such as $3x+7=19$ algebraically, and verifying the solution by substitution

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7A04 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: investigate, interpret and describe relationships between variables represented in graphs of functions developed from authentic data

elaborations.name: VC2M7A04-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using graphs to analyse a building’s electricity or gas usage over a period of time, the value of shares on a stock market, or the temperature during a day, interpreting and discussing the relationships they represent

elaborations.name: VC2M7A04-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using travel graphs to compare the distance travelled to and from school, interpreting and discussing features of travel graphs such as the slope of lines and the meaning of horizontal line segments

elaborations.name: VC2M7A04-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: telling the story behind what is being represented in graphs of functions, for example, graphs representing pouring rates or distance versus time

elaborations.name: VC2M7A04-E04 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using graphs of evaporation rates to explore and discuss Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples’ methods of water resource management

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7A05 - Mathematics

elaborations.name: VC2M7M01-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: using area formulas for rectangles and triangles to solve problems involving areas of surfaces

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7M02 - Mathematics

elaborations.name: VC2M7M02-E01 - Mathematics

elaborations.name: VC2M7M02-E02 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: developing the connection between the area of the parallel cross-section (base), the height and the volume of a rectangular or triangular prism to other prisms

elaborations.name: VC2M7M02-E03 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: connecting the area of the floor space and the number of floors of a high-rise building to calculate the volume of a building

elaborations.name: VC2M7M02-E04 - Mathematics

strand_content_descriptions.name: VC2M7M03 - Mathematics
strand_content_descriptions.text: describe the relationship between $\pi$ and the circumference, radius and diameter of a circle

elaborations.name: VC2M7M03-E01 - Mathematics
elaborations.elaboration_text: recognising the features of circles and their relationships to one another; for example, labelling the parts of a circle including centre, radius, diameter and circumference and using one of radius, diameter or circumference to determine the measure of the other 2; and understanding that the diameter of a circle is twice the radius, or that the radius is the circumference divided by $2\pi$

elaborations.elaboration_text: comparing the circumference of circles in relation to their radius and diameter with materials and measuring, to establish measurement formulas; for example, using a compass to draw several circles, then using string to approximate the circumference, comparing the length of string to the diameter of the circle

elaborations.name: VC2M7M03-E03 - Mathematics

elaborations.elaboration_text: investigating the applications and significance of circles in everyday life of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Peoples, such as in basketry, symbols and architecture, recognising the relationships between the centre, radius, diameter and circumference
